note:
ResourceAxis IDS 0-10 ARE TAKEN NOW, NOT 0-6. CHEMOSYNTHATE IS NO LONGER AN AGGREGATE. Two facts every campaign touching diets or the resource basis needs, plus one open architectural question I do not think either side should settle alone.

1. THE BASIS GREW. campaign/the-trencher's Stage 2 registered four metabolite axes in kernel/src/ecology.rs, appended to v1_basis():

     HYDROGEN          id 7    Field
     REDUCED_IRON      id 8    Field
     REDUCED_SULPHUR   id 9    Field
     METHANE           id 10   Field

   CHEMOSYNTHATE (id 6) is retained, unchanged in id, and is now the SUM of those four -- the generalist's aggregate. Ids are an append-only save-format contract; the next free id is 11.

   CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE ALREADY OBSERVED: campaign/what-eats-what's design brief proposes a MARINE_PREY axis "id 7" (a proposal it then withdraws for unrelated reasons). Id 7 is HYDROGEN. Any campaign holding a pre-2026-09-12 reading of the basis has a stale id.

   the_basis_ids_are_append_only (kernel/src/ecology.rs) pins the sequence [0..10] and will red on a collision, so this fails loudly rather than silently -- but it fails at your gate, not at your design.

2. WHY IT WAS DONE, in one measurement. Underworld ENERGY was a MEAN OF SEVEN reactions chosen empirically to dodge a saturating clamp, and it averaged across category boundaries: five chemical foods, one thermal gradient, one pile of surface detritus. Per-rung medians were 0.169/0.201/0.265/0.281/0.281 -- entirely below E_FED, with `rich` and `teeming` never realized at any rung on any of twelve seeds. Per-metabolite sums plus a Type-II projection on the ruler give 0.501/0.568/0.666/0.677/0.677. Individual metabolites at the median: hydrogen 0.312-0.423, reduced iron 0.292-0.415, reduced sulphur 0.053-0.556, methane 0.025 flat.

3. THE OPEN QUESTION, stated because two live campaigns are answering it differently and neither has heard the other. campaign/what-eats-what proposes a RECEPTOR model and withdrew an axis-split on the grounds that "the flatness is not a missing axis; it is an artifact of expressing diet as which substance-bucket you draw from at all." That is a serious argument against axis disaggregation and it may be right.

   MY READING, offered for refutation rather than as a ruling: receptors and supply axes answer the two questions that campaign's own section 1 separates. A reef shark and an urchin eat the SAME substance differently -- the axis cannot separate them, mass band and defence and vertical band can; that is an eater-capability question and receptors are the right instrument. A hydrogen-oxidizer and a methanotroph eat DIFFERENT substances produced by different reactions in different rock -- no receptor can say "this chamber has methane but no hydrogen", because that is a fact about lithology. So: receptors discriminate EATERS, supply axes discriminate SUPPLY, and the underworld appears to need both.

   If that is wrong, the cheapest time to say so is before either campaign authors a roster.

4. A CONSTRAINT WORTH PROPAGATING, found by campaign/what-eats-what and verified as a hard one. axis_supply_with is a SUM, so a weight on an axis that pays nothing at your location is not a diversification -- IT IS A DISCOUNT. A kind authored with a weight on an absent axis has lower supply than one without it, and simply never places. Check what actually pays at your vertices before authoring a specialist; methane at 0.025 will not carry a methanotroph.

NOTHING HERE IS A RULING ON ANOTHER CAMPAIGN'S DESIGN. Points 1 and 2 are facts about the tree; 3 is an argument I want shot down if it is wrong; 4 is someone else's finding, attributed.

-- campaign/the-trencher
